memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "He cast four gold rings for it and fastened them to its four feet, with two rings on one side and two rings on the other. Then he made poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with gold. And he inserted the poles into the rings on the sides of the ark to carry it." - Exod 37:3-5 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Rings and poles. God specified exactly how the ark would travel.

It was never to be carried in someone's arms, loaded onto a cart, or dragged. Poles ran through rings, and men carried it on their shoulders without ever touching the ark itself.

This mattered enormously. Centuries later, David tried moving the ark on a new cart — sincerely, joyfully, with music and celebration — and it ended in disaster (2 Sam 6:3-7). David later admitted the problem plainly: they had not enquired how to do it in the prescribed way (1 Chron 15:13).

Sincerity is not the same as obedience. Good intentions do not replace God's instructions. That is a hard word for a culture that treats sincerity as the highest virtue.

There is a gentler note here too. The poles meant the ark was always ready to move. Israel was a travelling people, and God's presence went with them, not left behind in a permanent building.

Wherever God has you going, His presence is portable. And however you serve Him, do it His way — the enthusiasm is not enough on its own.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where might you be serving God sincerely but not according to His Word?
2. Do you check what Scripture actually says, or rely on what feels right?
3. What comfort is there in knowing God's presence travels with you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, keep me from mistaking enthusiasm for obedience. Teach me to do Your work Your way. Amen.
